_source: Compiled from University of Ghana official entry requirements and general GTEC-referencing public-university admission guidance
_note: Aggregate bands below are of two kinds, marked explicitly per category: 'verified_example'/'verified_examples' means drawn from a specific cited cutoff case for a specific institution, programme and admission cycle; 'approximate_band' means a general guidance range, not any one institution's published cutoff. IMPORTANT, found while sourcing the 2026/2027 figures below: different news sources reported slightly different cut-offs for the SAME programme in the SAME cycle (e.g. KNUST Medicine was reported as aggregate 6 in one 2026/27 article and aggregate 7 in another, both citing KNUST's own release). This is real-world evidence that even 'verified' secondary-source figures can disagree, and is exactly why every verified_example below states its specific source and cycle rather than presenting one number as definitive. Neither kind should be presented to a user as a live, guaranteed-current cutoff - the system must state this distinction when answering, and must not imply a live CSSPS/university feed. None of this is historical admissions RECORDS (actual past admitted students' data) - that data is not publicly available anywhere; see docs/extending-data.md.

verified_examples: University of Ghana, 2026/2027 cycle: MBChB Medicine aggregate 8 (source: yen.com.gh reporting UG's published cut-off points, accessed 2026-10-16).

KNUST, 2026/2027 cycle: BSc Human Biology (Medicine) aggregate 7, Dentistry aggregate 9 or better (source: yen.com.gh reporting KNUST's entrance-exam announcement, accessed 2026-10-16). Note: a separate 2026/27 secondary source reported KNUST Medicine as aggregate 6 instead of 7 - the two disagree, which is itself the reason this is labeled a cited example rather than a guaranteed figure.
BSc Biomedical Engineering at University of Ghana, 2020/21 cycle: aggregate 9 with a minimum of B3 in Elective Mathematics. Cited as a specific historical case, not a current cutoff.

BSc Biomedical Engineering at University of Ghana, 2026/2027 cycle: aggregate 6 - the single most competitive cut-off UG published that cycle (source: yen.com.gh reporting UG's published cut-off points, accessed 2026-10-16). Notably lower than the 2020/21 figure above - a real example of how much a specific programme's cutoff can move cycle to cycle, which is exactly why a single number should never be treated as permanently current.
Doctor of Pharmacy at University of Ghana, 2026/2027 cycle: aggregate 10 (same source).
BSc Computer Science at University of Ghana, 2026/2027 cycle: aggregate 7 (source: yen.com.gh reporting UG's published cut-off points, accessed 2026-10-16).
BSc Administration at University of Ghana, 2026/2027 cycle: aggregate 9 (source: yen.com.gh reporting UG's published cut-off points, accessed 2026-10-16).
BA English and BA Sociology at University of Ghana, 2026/2027 cycle: both aggregate 18 (source: yen.com.gh reporting UG's published cut-off points, accessed 2026-10-16).

example_programmes: Entry-level eligibility for most public-university programmes
programme_categories.verified_example: GTEC-accredited public universities commonly cite aggregate 36 as the general floor, with mandatory C6+ in English, Core Mathematics, and the relevant third core subject — see mandatory_credit_gate in grading_scale.json. University of Ghana's own stated regular-admission ceiling is aggregate 24 (30 for Distance Education) — narrower than the general public-university floor, and itself an example of how this floor varies by institution.

options: any approved elective relevant to intended programme

programme_categories.caveat: Previously listed elective_min_grade as D7, which contradicted the mandatory credit-gate rule in grading_scale.json (D7 is a pass, not a credit). Corrected to C6 for the core-subject gate. Individual technical universities may set department-specific elective rules that differ from this; treat this row as the more conservative, general-floor assumption rather than a verified per-institution rule.
